title: Cabo – rules

rules.h1sub: Card game rules & how to play

sub: Peek, swap and remember: a quick memory card game for 2 to 5 players with a standard deck. Read it once, play a round, done.

seo.rulesT: Cabo Rules – How to Play the Card Game
seo.rulesD: Cabo with a standard deck explained: dealing, card values, peek, spy and swap powers, calling Cabo, scoring and variants.

goal: The goal: End each round with the lowest total of points in front of you. The catch: your four cards lie face down, and you only know them if you remember them.
setupLead: You need a standard 52-card deck without jokers and 2 to 5 players. A round takes only a few minutes.
dealP: Shuffle and deal 4 cards face down to each player. Without looking, everyone arranges their cards in a square of two rows in front of them.
setupAlt: In the middle lie the face-down draw pile and the face-up discard pile. In front of the player, four face-down cards in a square; the two nearest ones have been looked at.
lgPeekS: at the two cards nearest to you
setupP: Put the rest of the deck in the middle as the draw pile and turn its top card over to start the discard pile. Then everyone secretly looks at the two cards nearest to them – once only – and puts them back in place. From now on, memory is all you have.
valLead: Every card counts as many points as its number. Low cards are good, high cards are bad.
valP: Ace = 1, Jack = 11, Queen = 12. Kings are special: the black kings are the worst cards at 13 points, the red kings are the best at 0 points. Suits don’t matter otherwise.
turnLead: In the first round any player starts; after that, whoever had the lowest total in the previous round starts. Play goes clockwise. On your turn you take exactly one card – or you call “Cabo” instead (see Cabo!).
dq: Where do you take your card from?
bStockP: Look at the card without showing it. Then choose:
bStock1: Swap it for one of your cards: the new card goes face down in its place, the old one face up onto the discard pile.
bStock2: Discard it face up. If it’s a 7 to queen, you may use its power now.
bDiscP: Take the top card. You must swap it for one of your cards – the old card goes onto the discard pile. Powers don’t count here.
dnext: Then it’s the next player’s turn.
multiP: Do you think two or more of your cards have the same rank, for example two 5s? Then you can swap all of them for the one new card (whether from the draw or discard pile). Turn them face up: if they really match, they all go onto the discard pile and the new card takes one of their places. You now have fewer cards – great for your total.
multiAlt: A drawn 2 replaces two 5s from your own cards at once.
multiFail: If one card doesn’t match, you were wrong: turn the cards face down again in their places and add the new card face down to your cards as a penalty.
memP: You may only look at your face-down cards with a power. Leave every card where it lies, so you and everyone else can keep track of what is where.
powLead: The cards from 7 to queen have a power. You may only use it if you drew the card from the draw pile and discard it right away. Using the power is your whole turn.
pow7p: Look at one of your own face-down cards, then put it back.
pow9p: Look at one card of another player. Only you see it.
powJp: Swap any two cards on the table – yours or other players’ – without looking at them. Everyone sees where they go.
powKp: Kings can’t do anything. A black king is best discarded straight away, a red king is best kept.
powRhyme: A rhyme to remember: seven, eight – check your plate; nine, ten – peek at a friend; jack, queen – swap unseen.
caboLead: Once you think you have the lowest total at the table, you can end the round.
c1p: At the start of your turn, instead of taking a card, say “Cabo”. That’s your whole turn.
c2h: One last turn for everyone else
c2p: Each other player has one more normal turn. You don’t play any more, though the others may still spy on or swap your cards during their last turn.
c3p: Now everyone turns all their cards face up and adds up the points.
caboEmpty: If the draw pile runs out before anyone calls “Cabo”, the round ends at once and is scored the same way – without a caller.
scoreLead: After every round, write down the points. They add up from round to round.
score1: Everyone scores the total of their cards.
score2: The caller scores 0 if they have the lowest total, or share it.
score3: Is someone lower than the caller? Then the caller scores their total plus 10 penalty points.
exP: Mia has 6 points (the red king counts 0), Ben has 12. Mia is lowest, so she scores 0. Had Ben had only 5 points, Mia would have scored 6 + 10 = 16.
endP: Keep playing rounds until someone goes over 100 points. The game ends then, and the player with the lowest total wins. Hit exactly 100? Lucky you: your score drops to 50 – but only once per game.
varLead: Cabo is played in many ways. Agree before the first round which of these rules you use:
var1: Only one king at 0: Only the king of diamonds (the “one-eyed king”) counts 0; the other three kings count 13.
var2: Simpler swap: With a jack or queen you always swap one of your own cards with a card of another player.
var3: Older scoring: The lowest player always scores 0, even without calling. A caller who isn’t lowest only gets 5 penalty points instead of 10.
var4: Other start: Look at any two of your cards instead of the two nearest – or only at one, for a harder game.
var5: Throw in at any time: As soon as a card lands on the discard pile, anyone who has a card of the same rank may throw it on top. A wrong guess costs a penalty card. This rule is typical of Cambio.
var6: Empty draw pile: Instead of ending the round, shuffle the discard pile (except its top card) and keep playing.
var7: With jokers: Add the two jokers; they count 0 points and have no power.
var8: Kamikaze: Whoever finishes the round with two queens and two black kings (two 12s and two 13s) scores 0 points – and everyone else scores 50.
faq1q: Can I look at my cards again later?
faq1a: No. After the start, you only see your own cards with a 7 or 8 – or when you discard them. Everything else you have to remember.
faq2q: Can I use a power if I take the card from the discard pile?
faq2a: No. Powers only work with cards from the draw pile that you discard straight away. From the discard pile you always have to swap.
faq3q: Can I keep a 7 instead of using its power?
faq3a: Yes. Then you simply swap it for one of your cards, and it counts 7 points at the end like any other card.
faq4a: There is no fixed rule. If you are fairly sure you have only a few points – around 5 or less – it is often a good moment. But remember the 10 penalty points if someone else is lower.
faq5q: What happens if a player has no cards left?
faq5a: In the basic Cabo rules you always keep at least one card, because a new card replaces the ones you swap out. If you play with the house rule Throw in at any time and end up with no cards left, your total is 0 – you can’t go any lower, so you are hard to beat in that round.
faq6q: Is Cabo the same as Cambio?
faq6a: They are close relatives. The idea is the same, and the game is also known as Pablo or Cactus. The details differ from table to table – Cambio, for example, usually lets everyone throw matching cards onto the discard pile at any time (see Variants).
faq7a: Yes, Cabo also exists as a commercial card game with its own deck, created in 2010 by Melissa Limes and Mandy Henning. This page explains how to play with a standard deck of cards.
